doc.title: Rick Montalbano interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 12, 2011

chapter: Lou Rawls band, Alias and Jaco
title: Playing with local horn sections and adapting on the Rawls tours
summary: The band often used local players or Buddy Rich's horn section, and Montalbano adjusted his organ playing to sit in the mix.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: A lot of those gigs, you had a core rhythm section and if it was going to be a large band and you would go to a town and there would be the local guys filling the chairs?

Yeah. Well we were fortunate. Sometimes we played a lot in New York and it was always Buddy Rich’s horn section and you’d get some good bands on the west coast and here and there. Sometimes it was a little tough but, you know, we were together. We were a unit so we made it work. We could have made it work without the big band. And we did, night after night. So it wasn’t that much of a problem that the band was not that together.
I’ll bet you had to adjust your playing.
Yeah. It was lot less organ, you know bigger organ sounds, and it was a lot more stepping back a little bit, you know, into the mix.
